reviews.name: Backpack
reviews.reason: Backpack identity and Garden colors read cleanly, but the selected/card pixels show a flat rounded front panel with emblem-like decoration rather than a dimensional bag. Add body thickness, strap/zipper/seam construction, fabric response and three-quarter collectible lighting while keeping Tier 1 simple and friendly.

reviews.name: Mini Pack
reviews.reason: The compact purple pack and star cue are readable, but the object remains a shallow front-facing icon. Galaxy Glow is mostly palette and badge; the pack needs believable side depth, hardware/pocket construction, textile highlights and spatial lighting without overcomplicating Starter tier.

reviews.name: Controller Pack
reviews.reason: Controller-pack identity is unmistakable and card-readable, but the controller and backpack are stacked flat shapes. Sunny Pop is background-led rather than materially expressed; add bag thickness, controller mounting depth, molded controls, seams and directional highlights.

reviews.name: Bunny Bag
reviews.reason: The bunny-face/ears make this distinct and appealing, but it still reads like a mascot icon printed on a card. Give the bag real plush/synthetic-material volume, ear attachment, zipper/strap depth and Aqua Wave material accents with coherent three-quarter lighting.

reviews.name: Leaf Pack
reviews.reason: Leaf-pack silhouette and botanical emblem are readable, but the bag remains flat and Art Attack is weakly expressed beyond colored dots/waves. Add dimensional pack construction, layered leaf material, pockets/hardware and more specific art-supply or painted-material storytelling.

reviews.name: Rocket Pack
reviews.reason: Rocket-pack identity and flame pods are clear, but the body is a flat front panel with symmetrical side blocks. Star Luxe needs convincing metal volume/reflection, nozzles/fasteners, depth-separated components and richer controlled hero lighting.

reviews.name: Skate Pack
reviews.reason: The skateboard strapped across the pack differentiates the item, but the card still reads as layered flat vector shapes beneath the locked state. Tier 3 needs believable deck/truck/wheel and pack attachment depth, textile/board materials and neon rim-lighting rather than color bands alone.

reviews.name: Bubble Tank
reviews.reason: Tank/bubble identity reads, but transparency is depicted with simple flat circles/gradients and little refraction or shell thickness. Build an actual dimensional transparent tank, frame/hoses/attachment structure, candy-like material accents and stronger spatial highlights.

reviews.name: Art Supply Pack
reviews.reason: Brushes and art-pack purpose are legible, but the construction is front-facing and flat, while Adventure Club is not strongly carried by the materials or accessory arrangement. Add real pouch/strap depth, protruding tools with occlusion, rugged travel-art materials and directional lighting.

reviews.name: Wing Pack
reviews.reason: Wing-pack silhouette is clear, but Tier 4 remains a symmetric flat icon: the wings are simple outlined lobes and the central pack has little engineering/material depth. Add articulated/feathered or molded wing construction, mounting hardware, cloud-soft materials and richer high-tier lighting.

reviews.name: Cloud Wings
reviews.reason: Cloud-wing identity, central gem and pixel motifs are distinct, but the wings are broad flat vector masses. Tier 4 needs plush/volumetric cloud lobes, spatial layering, translucent/pixel-light accents and stronger front-to-back construction instead of motif-only complexity.

reviews.name: Star Wings
reviews.reason: The final-tier wings are colorful and more spectacular than lower tiers, but still use a flat symmetric vector language with limited feather/structure thickness, material response and environmental light. Tier 5 needs a genuinely luxe dimensional wing build, layered depth and controlled hero sparkle/glow while preserving Berry Blast readability.
